scope: Theorem 3.1 (Ren–Wang, discrete form) of the manuscript “Bochner–Riesz multipliers in three dimensions” (preprints/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026/Bochner-Riesz-Multipliers-in-Three-Dimensions-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 078 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ea18d159eefcdc7f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 0 < s ≤ 1, 0 < d ≤ 2, and α > 0. There are η0 = η0(α, s, d) > 0 and ρ0 = ρ0(α, s, d) > 0 with the following property. Suppose P is a nonempty (ρ, d, ρ−η0 )-set of squares, with 0 < ρ < ρ0. For each p ∈ P, let T (p) be a family of tubes meeting p, of cardinality comparable to M, and forming a (ρ, s, ρ−η0 )-set. Then # [ p∈P T (p) ≳α ρ− min{1,d,(d+s)/2}+α M. (3.1) The statement is unchanged by fixed bounded domains, finitely many coordinate charts, or fixed- factor enlargements of the grids and tubes, after decreasing η0, ρ0 if necessary.
